clue.text: Decline energy drink, husband having complaint

parts.note: go is energy or get-up-and-go
to down is to drink in one
an ill is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their energy drink once the husband falls sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate steadily is an idiom for worsening, which is what declining means here as a verb.

clue.text: Image PC may have over time, becoming bent

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a GIF is an image file format found on computers

explanation.surface: A picture on a computer warps over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is the noun, a natural aptitude, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural talent or flair, a synonym for an innate aptitude.

clue.text: Wipe floor with pad father's left — then polish

indicators.note: left means departed, so the father's letters go from the word pad and what remains is used

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: Domestic instructions: clean the floor with a pad, then shine it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipe floor with' sounds like cleaning but is slang for thrashing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a crushing defeat: to wipe the floor with an opponent is to thrash them.

clue.text: Motto's wise words an introduction to heroism originally

indicators.note: originally suggests the letters were once in another order and have been rearranged
an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of heroism is taken

explanation.surface: A slogan sums up wisdom as a starting point for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses the letters of 'wise words an' plus H, the first letter of 'heroism'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the motto of the SAS, the British Army's special forces regiment.

clue.text: Little one forgets about a girl

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so the letter for about is dropped

parts.note: a child is a little one
C is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A small child loses track of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilda is a girl's name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Scottish town to embrace before touring British Isles

parts.note: to lock someone in your arms is to embrace them

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for before goes around the letters for British Isles

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
BI abbreviates British Isles

explanation.surface: A travel note: a Scottish town to hug before a tour of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockerbie is a small town in Dumfriesshire, south-west Scotland, an example of a Scottish settlement.

clue.text: Leaves of orange falling from September at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so the opening letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: An autumnal scene: orange foliage dropping as September begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb: someone who offs leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To off is a colloquial verb for going away, so offs is a slangy synonym for departs.

clue.text: Doctor more of an extremely unhelpful sort of GP

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged
extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters U and L of unhelpful

explanation.surface: A complaint about a family doctor who is even more unhelpful than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like a general practitioner, a family doctor, but here means Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: A Formula One race is a kind of Grand Prix, so it is an example of that motor-racing event.

clue.text: Where spectators are keen to have a go at champion

parts.note: the stand at a sports ground is where the spectators are

parts.words: keen to have a go at
parts.note: up for means eager to try something

explanation.surface: In the stands, fans are eager to take on the champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion here is a verb: to champion a cause is to defend or support it publicly.

clue.text: Officer commanding us in the Suffolks perhaps for a time

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the group of sheep

parts.note: Suffolk is a breed of sheep, so a group of them is a flock
us gives our, the possessive form of the first person plural
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: An officer is in charge of soldiers in the Suffolk Regiment for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Suffolks' suggests the old county regiment; in fact it is a breed of sheep, and sheep form a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour on the clock, such as tea-time, is an example of a time of day.

clue.text: Patch threadbare acrylic pockets

indicators.note: pockets means holds within, so the letters are concealed inside threadbare acrylic

explanation.surface: A worn synthetic garment has pockets, or needs patching.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch of ground is a synonym for a stretch or region of land.

clue.text: Kept going over cape, brightly coloured, with scissors, roughly cutting

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the rearranged letters go inside the colour

parts.note: red is a bright colour

indicators.note: roughly means imprecisely, so the letters of scissors are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hacks roughly at a bright cloak with scissors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brightly coloured' looks like a description of the cape, but it is the colour piece that the scrambled scissors cut into.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that run back and forth across something repeatedly are said to go over it again and again.

clue.text: Place for drill clip holding plug attached to earth

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the trimming word wraps round the advert

parts.note: to pare is to trim or clip
a plug is an advertisement, an ad
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: Electrical instructions: a clip holding a plug is connected to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' and 'earth' suggest power tools and wiring; the drill is military marching.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers practise marching drill on an open square kept for that purpose.

clue.text: Light verse competition in which hatred's kept quiet

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the hatred word goes within the contest

parts.note: a slam is a poetry contest where verses are performed
odium is hatred or loathing
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: At a poetry contest, simmering animosity is held in check, and quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective describing the verse; it is the noun, a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sodium lamp is a type of street lighting with a yellow glow, an example of a lamp.

clue.text: Like it or not boy, in two years there'll be nothing left

parts.note: Will is a boy's name

indicators.note: in means placed between, so the nothing and left letters sit within the two years
two means the year letter appears twice

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A warning to a lad: whether you like it or not, in two years nothing will remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whether one wishes it or not, so it is a synonym for regardless of preference.

clue.text: There were no survivors except for revolutionary in military uniform

parts.note: read as zero lived, with the letter O standing for zero

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for except is read backwards

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A grim tale: nobody survived except a rebel in army dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There were no survivors' is read literally as nought lived, O LIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull greenish-brown colour of army fatigues, used for the uniform itself.

clue.text: People sounding rough on the phone — hope for better?

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: on the phone one only hears words, so the next word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a voice that sounds rough is hoarse

explanation.surface: Someone with a croaky voice on a call hopes things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, a punter, not a comparative of good.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter backing an animal in a race pins their hopes on it, so it is a gambler's hope.

clue.text: Tart's flat's opposite

definitions.meaning: in music, the note raised a semitone is the opposite of a flat

explanation.surface: A sour-tasting flat-dweller is contrasted with its counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a sour taste is keen and acidic, and in music the raised note contrasts with the lowered one.

clue.text: Home Rule one brought closer with Act of Union

definitions.text: one brought closer with Act of Union

parts.note: in means at home
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Irish Home Rule and the Act of Union are set against each other, as in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act of Union' evokes the 1800 union of Great Britain and Ireland, but here means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage becomes family through a wedding, the union that links two families.

clue.text: Concedes right to play, rising from piano?

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters are loose and free to move about

explanation.surface: Someone yields the right to perform, getting up from the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical marking for soft, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a gradual increase in loudness starting from a soft passage is a swelling.

clue.text: Satellite image, apparently of jogger, leg coming round a fraction

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the fraction phrase goes inside

parts.note: a memo jogs the memory
a ninth is a fraction
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A satellite picture shows a jogger whose leg is wrapping round part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogger' looks like a runner but is a memory-jogger, a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon is Earth's satellite, and the face people claim to see on it is an apparent image.

clue.text: Ammo — bullets — regularly bringing shed down?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Ammunition is used up as bullets bring down a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is soft feathers, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds lose feathers seasonally, so the verb for that is a fitting way to say lose plumage.

clue.text: This very minute stick broken by spades

indicators.note: broken by means split open by, so the card suit letter goes inside

parts.note: to jut is to stick out
S is the abbreviation for spades in cards

explanation.surface: A stick is smashed with spades this instant.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb as in just now means a moment ago or at this moment, so it fits the time phrase.

clue.text: From bouquet picked up European flower

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a bouquet is a fragrance or smell

explanation.surface: A European bloom is chosen from a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river, not a bloom; 'bouquet' is a scent, not a bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder runs along the Germany–Poland border, so it is a European river.

clue.text: Recover after sacrificing queen to achieve mate

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, so the queen's letter is removed

parts.note: to rally is to recover
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A chess player bounces back after giving up the queen to deliver checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like checkmate but means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a friend or partner, and a partner on your side is a synonym.

clue.text: German woman detective Yard used in this?

parts.note: Frau is German for woman or wife
DS is a detective sergeant
a quad is a quadrangle, an enclosed yard

explanation.surface: A German woman detective works with Scotland Yard on the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters; here it is a quadrangle. 'used' means conned.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers investigating deception deal with cases where people are cheated or duped.

clue.text: Drama after Lord's opener's pulled stumps up

indicators.note: pulled means withdrawn, so the opening letter is taken out

parts.note: drama as a genre is plays

indicators.note: an opener is the first, so the first letter of Lord's is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket match at Lord's ends when the opening batsman is out and the umpires remove the bails.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; to pull stumps is to end play, but 'stumps up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump up is British slang for paying money, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Creator of files communist dictator got about former fifties Youth Resistance

indicators.note: got about means surrounded, so the dictator's name goes round the next pieces

parts.note: Tito led communist Yugoslavia
an ex is a former partner
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth subculture member
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Cold War tale: a communist strongman surrounds former Teddy boys in the resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Software for writing plain files is a program that produces documents.
